title: German Chancellor Merz Faces Political Crisis After Election Losses
subtitle: The leader vows to continue his reform agenda despite major defeats at the state level.

summary.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is under intense pressure after his party suffered significant losses in recent state elections. The far-right AfD party and the far-left Die Linke party both achieved strong results in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin. Despite calls for him to step down, Merz has promised to remain in office to lead the country. He argues that his planned reforms are necessary for Germany's democratic future. Political experts suggest that the country is experiencing a major shift in its traditional party system.
summary.zh: 德國總理梅爾茲在所屬政黨於近期邦議會選舉中慘敗後，正面臨巨大壓力。極右派的德國另類選擇黨與極左派的左派黨，在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦與柏林皆取得強勢表現。儘管外界呼籲他下台，梅爾茲仍承諾留任並領導國家。他主張其規劃的改革對德國的民主未來至關重要。政治專家認為，德國正經歷傳統政黨體系的重大轉變。

paragraphs.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is facing a difficult political crisis following a series of poor results for his party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), in recent state elections. Instead of traveling to the United Nations General Assembly as planned, the Chancellor remained in Berlin to address the situation after his party suffered its worst election performance since World War II.
paragraphs.zh: 德國總理梅爾茲（Friedrich Merz）正面臨嚴峻的政治危機，起因於他的所屬政黨「基督教民主聯盟」（CDU）近期在多場邦議會選舉中表現慘澹。總理原定前往聯合國大會，但為了處理選後局勢，他選擇留在柏林，因為該黨遭遇了自第二次世界大戰以來最嚴重的選舉挫敗。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the CDU failed to reach the 5% threshold—the minimum percentage of votes required to enter the local parliament—in the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. This result was particularly shocking because the region was once a stronghold for his party. Meanwhile, in Berlin, the CDU fell to second place behind the far-left Die Linke party. These losses come only two weeks after a crushing defeat in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, which first triggered serious questions about the Chancellor's future.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，基民盟在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦（Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania）的得票率未能達到進入當地議會所需的百分之五最低門檻。此結果格外令人震驚，因為該地區曾是該黨的鐵票倉。與此同時，在柏林，基民盟的得票率落後於極左派的「左派黨」（Die Linke），退居第二。這些敗績發生在薩克森-安哈特邦（Saxony-Anhalt）慘敗的兩週後，該次挫敗首度引發外界對總理未來動向的嚴重質疑。

paragraphs.en: Despite the pressure, Merz has dismissed speculation that he might resign. Speaking on Monday, he vowed to keep his coalition government together, stating that his focus is on the country’s "democratic future." He described the election results as a "disaster" but insisted that he would continue with his federal agenda of tax and welfare reforms. Merz argued that these changes are the "antidote to the poison of authoritarianism" and that implementing them requires "backbone, steadfastness and patience."
paragraphs.zh: 儘管壓力沉重，梅爾茲仍駁斥了關於他可能辭職的臆測。他在週一發言時誓言維持聯合政府運作，並表示他的重心在於國家的「民主未來」。他將選舉結果形容為一場「災難」，但堅持會繼續推動聯邦層級的稅務與福利改革議程。梅爾茲主張，這些變革是「對抗威權主義毒素的解藥」，而落實這些政策需要「骨氣、堅定與耐心」。

paragraphs.en: NPR reports that the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party has made significant gains, securing 38.2% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. The party’s leaders have been vocal in their criticism of the Chancellor, with AfD candidate Leif-Erik Holm predicting that the "twilight of the chancellor’s era has begun." Alice Weidel, the federal leader of the AfD, claimed that the more the Chancellor tries to stay in power, the more her party benefits.
paragraphs.zh: 美國公共廣播電台（NPR）報導指出，極右派的「德國另類選擇黨」（AfD）取得了顯著斬獲，在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦拿下百分之三十八點二的選票。該黨領袖對總理大加撻伐，另類選擇黨候選人霍爾姆（Leif-Erik Holm）預言「總理時代的黃昏已經降臨」。該黨聯邦領袖魏德爾（Alice Weidel）則聲稱，總理越是試圖保住權力，她的政黨就越能從中獲益。

paragraphs.en: In Berlin, the political landscape is also shifting. The far-left Die Linke party achieved its best result ever with 25.7% of the vote. Their lead candidate, Elif Eralp, has promised to make the city more affordable by introducing a rent cap and potentially taking control of apartments owned by large real estate companies. Eralp stated that the people of Berlin will not tolerate the policies of the AfD, adding that "love and justice have triumphed over hate" in the city.
paragraphs.zh: 在柏林，政治版圖也正在變動。極左派的左派黨以百分之二十五點七的得票率，創下該黨史上最佳成績。他們的領軍候選人埃拉爾普（Elif Eralp）承諾，將透過實施租金上限，並可能將大型房地產公司持有的公寓收歸公有，讓城市生活更為平價。埃拉爾普表示，柏林市民絕不會容忍另類選擇黨的政策，並補充說「愛與正義已在該市戰勝了仇恨」。

paragraphs.en: While regional leaders of the CDU have offered their support to Merz, it remains unclear how long this backing will last. Many observers note that there are few candidates currently willing to take over the position, which is increasingly being described as a "poisoned chalice"—a role that brings more trouble than reward. Merz himself suggested that these election results are not just a personal failure, but a sign of a "profound transformation" in the political systems of Germany and other countries around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然基民盟的區域領袖已對梅爾茲表達支持，但這份支持能持續多久仍是未知數。許多觀察家指出，目前幾乎沒有候選人願意接手這個職位，該職位正被形容為「有毒的聖杯」，意指這是一個弊大於利的職務。梅爾茲本人則暗示，這些選舉結果不僅是個人的失敗，更是德國及全球其他國家政治體系「深刻轉型」的徵兆。

paragraphs.en: As the country moves forward, the focus will be on whether the Chancellor can successfully manage his coalition partners. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the Social Democrats (SPD) are expected to lead a new government. Their state leader, Manuela Schwesig, focused her campaign on acting as a barrier against the AfD. Because the German electoral system uses a mix of winner-take-all and proportional representation, parties must often form coalitions—agreements between different groups to work together—to govern effectively. Whether these new local governments can stabilize the political situation remains the primary question for the coming months.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著國家持續前進，焦點將在於總理能否成功駕馭他的聯合政府夥伴。在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦，社會民主黨（SPD）預計將主導新政府。該邦領袖施韋西格（Manuela Schwesig）將競選主軸定調為擔任對抗另類選擇黨的防線。由於德國選舉制度結合了勝者全拿與比例代表制，各政黨通常必須組成聯合政府——即不同團體間為有效治理而達成的合作協議。這些新成立的地方政府能否穩定政治局勢，仍是未來幾個月的主要課題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A place where a particular group or belief is very popular or influential.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 大本營、據點，指某個政黨或勢力在該地非常有影響力。
keyTerms.noteZh: 此詞常指軍事上的堡壘，這裡指政治上的優勢選區。文中：This result was particularly shocking because the region was once a stronghold for his party.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Strength of character; the courage to do what is right.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是脊椎，這裡引申為面對困難時的堅毅性格。文中：Merz argued that these changes are the "antidote to the poison of authoritarianism" and that implementing them requires "backbone, steadfastness and patience."

keyTerms.definitionEn: A position or role that seems attractive but actually brings more trouble and difficulty than reward.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 看似誘人但實則充滿麻煩與災難的職位（毒酒杯）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個隱喻用法，形容權力位置帶來的負擔。文中：Many observers note that there are few candidates currently willing to take over the position, which is increasingly being described as a "poisoned chalice"—a role that brings more trouble than reward.

quiz.question: What specific election outcome in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania is highlighted as particularly surprising for the CDU?

options.A: They were defeated by the Social Democrats (SPD).
options.B: They failed to meet the minimum vote percentage required to enter the local parliament.
options.C: They received fewer votes than the far-right AfD party.
options.D: They lost their status as the primary governing party for the first time since World War II.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，CDU 在 Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania 未能達到 5% 的得票門檻，這對曾經是該黨大本營的地區來說是令人震驚的結果。選項 A 雖然提到 SPD 將領導新政府，但並非該段落強調的 CDU 失敗原因。選項 C 雖然 AfD 確實獲得了 38.2% 的高票，但文章強調的是 CDU 未達門檻的事實。選項 D 說法過於誇大，文章僅提到這是該黨自二戰以來最慘烈的表現，而非首次失去執政地位。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might the CDU struggle to find a replacement for Friedrich Merz if he were to resign?

options.A: The party is currently banned from participating in national elections.
options.B: The coalition government has legally forbidden any leadership changes.
options.C: The position is perceived as having more negative consequences than benefits.
options.D: There is a lack of qualified candidates within the party who support tax reforms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第六段提到該職位被描述為「毒酒杯」（poisoned chalice），意指這是一個帶來的麻煩遠多於回報的角色，因此很少有人願意接手。選項 A 文章並未提及黨派被禁。選項 B 文章未提到法律禁止更換領導人。選項 D 雖然提到改革，但文章強調的是職位本身的風險，而非缺乏支持改革的候選人。

quiz.question: In the context of the article, what does the phrase 'poisoned chalice' imply about the role of the Chancellor?

options.A: A position that is highly prestigious but requires dangerous travel.
options.B: A leadership role that is undesirable due to the severe problems attached to it.
options.C: A temporary office that must be surrendered after a short period.
options.D: A political appointment that is intentionally sabotaged by coalition partners.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在第六段中，作者使用「poisoned chalice」（毒酒杯）這一隱喻，解釋了為何儘管 Merz 面臨壓力，黨內卻鮮少有人願意取代他，因為這個職位目前充滿了政治危機與難題，接手者將面臨極大風險。選項 A 錯誤，因為該詞強調的是麻煩而非榮耀。選項 C 與 D 均非該隱喻在文中的核心含義，文中並未暗示該職位是臨時的或遭到特定盟友蓄意破壞。

quiz.question: What is the central theme of this article regarding the current state of German politics?

options.A: The successful implementation of tax and welfare reforms by the coalition government.
options.B: The total collapse of the far-left Die Linke party in major German cities.
options.C: The rise of extreme political parties and the resulting instability for the Chancellor's government.
options.D: The personal failure of Friedrich Merz to manage the United Nations General Assembly.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體探討了 CDU 在選舉中的慘敗、極右翼 AfD 的崛起以及極左翼 Die Linke 的勢力消長，這些因素共同導致了德國政治局勢的不穩定，並直接威脅到總理 Merz 的領導地位。選項 A 與文意相反，改革尚未成功。選項 B 與事實不符，Die Linke 在柏林取得了史上最好成績。選項 D 僅是開頭的一個小細節，並非文章的核心主旨。
